findings.1: **1. The git half's name set is pinned by nothing (medium).** `main()` calls `hook_run(hook_texts, top_names)`, and ad23a96 put `all_names` one identifier away in the same scope. Changing that argument to `all_names` leaves the suite at 46/46: the case "a hook declaring a skill's script is reported, not read as a guard" calls `m.hook_run` directly with a hand-passed `{"in-scripts"}`, so it pins the function and not the wiring. Probed: `hook_run({"pre-commit": "# runs: campaign-role-brief.py"}, all_names)` returns `({'campaign-role-brief.py'}, [])` -- a guard git can never run, announced as installed, problem line gone. Worse direction. Wants a case through `main()`.
findings.2: **2. `.claude/settings.local.json` is still missed (low-medium).** The harness reads it above `.claude/settings.json`; one exists at `/Users/hyungmokim/campaign-base/.claude/settings.local.json` (`.gitignore:19`), today permissions only. A hook registered there runs unannounced, the direction this commit fixes, and "There are two such files" is what goes stale. Adding it costs an extra `!!` in most checkouts, so weigh making an absent *project* file silence. Alone the changed absent-file line is factual, not a false alarm.
findings.3: **3. Dropping `top and` (note, accept).** No basename collides across `scripts/` and the three skill roots today. With a planted collision both copies get announced -- an over-call, the better direction; `top and` would have under-called the skill copy.

label.evidence: read by hand at comment 5565306719 against comment 5565400702
label.rule: four bold defect paragraphs and the 'Stale, user-visible' item; the REPORT's 9-row table disposes each

findings.item1: **R3 lost coverage the deny list had, on the two spellings its own comments named.** One mutation in `install-hooks.sh` (`"$root/scripts/campaign-bound"`, `"$BASE/scripts/campaign-claim.py" stood-down "$N"`): main's guard 2 findings, this branch 0. `SCRIPT_CALL`'s `(?<![\w./-])` blocks every `$BASE/scripts/…`; `CLAIM_CALL`'s lookahead fails on a quoted argument. So R3a sees 0 of the skills' 19 `$BASE/scripts/` sites; R3b misses `d / "runtime" / "claims"`; R3c sees 3 tokens tree-wide, 2 of them prose in refusal strings.
findings.item2: **The hook's two non-zero branches are pinned by nothing.** `1) exit 0` → `1) ;;`: 37/37 pass. `*)` push-anyway → `*) exit 0`: 37/37 pass. The `--is-claim` cases pin the answerer, not the hook; both "never reaches the remote" cases pass because pre-commit refuses first.
findings.item3: **`--is-claim` answers by exit status, and 1 is also Python's crash code.** `answer()` guards nothing round `claim_on`: any uncaught exception exits 1, the hook reads "no", the push is skipped — the failure the comment says it prevents. (git-missing is fine: probed, exit 2.)
findings.item4: **`campaign_prefixes` returning `[]` widens rather than narrows.** `read_branches(refspec=[])` is `for-each-ref` with no pattern (32 refs here, 0 scoped) and `read_worktrees(prefix=())` disables its filter, while the note printed says no claim appears. `cmd_release` is safe.
findings.item5: **Stale, user-visible:** `campaign-token-tally.py --help` prints "both forms are matched"; also `--campaign`'s "in branch names", `known_slugs` and `cmd_release` docstrings.

REPORT machinery-worker-10: fix round 1 at `9177efe` — four behavioural defects fixed in one commit, five findings dispositioned, four REPORT claims corrected. Landed rule applied.

| finding | kind | disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R3's lookbehind blocked a preceding slash, so every `$BASE/scripts/...` was invisible and R3 was **narrower than the deny list it replaced** | **behavioural, in a shipped guard** | **fixed.** Verified the reviewer's two probes myself against the compiled patterns before touching anything. The lookbehind now excludes a glued word only; `RUNTIME_CALL` regains `d / "runtime" / "claims"`, the shape the deleted entry's own comment named; R3c's lookahead admits a quoted argument. Four cases, one per pattern plus the glued-word allow |
| `--is-claim` carries its verdict in the exit status alone, and 1 is also python's crash code | **behavioural** | **fixed.** It leads with a word (`claim` / `no-claim` / `unknown`), wraps `claim_on`, and the hook believes the word. A word and a status that disagree are themselves an unread question |
| `campaign_prefixes` returning `[]` **widened** the sweep — no `for-each-ref` pattern, and `read_worktrees`'s `if prefix and` guard disabled — while the note said no claim would appear | **behavioural** | **fixed.** Neither runs on an empty list. One case on the consequence, not the return value; the mutation that reverts it reddens exactly that case |
| the push hook's two non-zero branches are pinned by nothing | **a test that passes with its branch deleted** | **fixed.** Three cases stub the reader in the worktree's own copy — the one the hook resolves — and pin what the hook does with each word. The earlier cases were satisfied by the pre-commit half refusing first, which is the reviewer's point exactly |
| `claim_subcommands()`'s unnamed fourth outcome (readable, empty set) | latent | **fixed** in the same commit: `if subs` reads it as could-not-look |
| `--slug`/`--campaign` help and two comments still promise the retired fallback | refinement, user-visible | **fixed** in the same commit |
| `extensionless_call()` is dead code | refinement | **deleted.** R3a covers it |
| R3a's suite stand-down costs 21 findings; marking them restores it | refinement | **accepted as is.** All 33 are fixture noise (`scripts/gone.py` is the point of the case it sits in). The stand-down is counted and printed on every run, so it is loud rather than silent; 33 markers of churn buy nothing measured |
| `prefixes()` keeps a parameter it `del`s | refinement | **accepted as is.** Every caller has it and the empty-case message names that campaign |

**Four claims of mine the reviewer re-derived and corrected — all conceded.**

1. "every `<slug>/` claim cut since #181 committed without ever being pushed." False. Three slug branches exist and #241/#242 were pushed by hand or before this change. The hook did not push them; the true statement is that it never would have.
2. "Old glob back → two named cases." One, not two (36/37).
3. "the cases were renamed with the code, so they pass under either name." **Better than I reported**: reverting the two section tuples fails 15 of 115 tracker cases. My probe was still the right check — it just was not the only cover.
4. "#1's and #237's bodies still carry `## Done when`." So do 31 of 138 closed issues, and `check --plan` refuses each. Since `campaign-claim take` calls it, **claiming a reopened old sub-issue now costs a planner edit first**. Filed on #237 rather than fixed here: it is a migration of issue bodies, not a code defect, and the owner is editing #1 and #237 by hand already.

1,370 cases, 0 failures. `check-tree-shape`, `check-rule-readers`, `check-cross-references` clean (153 references, 0 dangling, 0 undecided).

**A narrowed review at `9177efe` is asked for**, on this round's diff alone (`7d10745..9177efe`). This push retired the review at `7d10745`.
